# Transistor

- Category: host
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://transistor.fm/, https://developers.transistor.fm/, https://support.transistor.fm/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md). **Where this file and `vendors.md` differ, `vendors.md` is authoritative.**

## Integration surface

- **API:** REST, JSON:API spec, `x-api-key` header auth, read/write. Resources: User, Show, Episode, Subscriber, ShowAnalytics, EpisodeAnalytics/EpisodesAnalytics, AudioUpload (presigned uploads), Webhook. Rate limit 10 req/10s (429 + 10s block on excess). [developers.transistor.fm](https://developers.transistor.fm/) (2026-09-26)
- **Webhooks:** 4 events — `episode_created`, `episode_published`, `subscriber_created`, `subscriber_deleted` — managed via `GET/POST /v1/webhooks` and `DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id`. [developers.transistor.fm](https://developers.transistor.fm/) (2026-09-26)
- **Export formats:** Standard RSS feed (industry-portable); transcripts exportable/linkable as SRT/VTT/JSON/TXT/HTML via `podcast:transcript`; no documented bulk CSV/analytics export beyond API calls — undocumented.
- **SSO / auth:** No SSO/SAML documentation found on transistor.fm, developers.transistor.fm, or support.transistor.fm as of this check — undocumented (likely a manual "contact sales" item at Enterprise, but that is not stated anywhere public).
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) RSS feed cannot use a custom domain — it always lives on `feeds.transistor.fm`, so the feed URL itself is Transistor-branded until you redirect away; (2) analytics are Transistor's own IAB-guideline-compliant but **not IAB-certified** methodology, so historical download numbers may not map cleanly onto a certified competitor if you migrate; (3) free permanent 301 redirect exists for leaving, which mitigates feed lock-in; (4) comments/community depends entirely on the Bluesky integration — there's no native commenting system, so that "community" feature is really a third-party dependency, not portable data.

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Transistor covers most of Relay's checklist reasonably well for a single-vendor buy: unlimited multi-show hosting with a network site, per-podcast RBAC (Owner/Admin/Member/Analytics), private feeds at every tier, a real read/write API with webhooks, and `podcast:transcript` support. Gaps matter for Relay's specific bar: there is no documented approval-before-publish/editorial workflow — Admin/Member can publish directly — so Relay's "immutable release record with review gates" would have to be built on top via the API. Its Apple Podcasts HLS video support is real but still waitlisted/gradual, not GA. Analytics are IAB-guideline-compliant but not certified, a possible credibility gap for advertisers. "Community" is just a Bluesky-replies bridge, not a native membership/discussion feature. Custom RSS domains are unsupported (a portability constraint, offset by free 301 redirects). For the 2-show pilot with video, Professional ($49/mo) is the cheapest fit, because video is a Professional-and-above beta.

## Research notes

- `https://transistor.fm/features/custom-domains/` returned HTTP 404; used `support.transistor.fm` articles on custom domains instead.
- No page found stating SSO/SAML support one way or the other; treated as undocumented rather than assuming Enterprise-only.
- Could not find Transistor on the IAB Tech Lab's own compliant-companies certificate list (searched, not independently browsed page-by-page); relying on Transistor's own support-article statement that it is compliant but not certified.
- Pricing figures ("20K", "100K", "250K" downloads/mo) are as displayed on the pricing page in quotes in Transistor's own copy; exact plan mechanics (e.g., what happens over the cap) were not explicitly stated on the fetched page.
- Transcript manual-editing capability (vs. paste/upload only) is not explicitly confirmed in either direction — marked undocumented.
- Apple Podcasts HLS video partner status confirmed both from Transistor's own page and third-party coverage (Podnews/Sounds Profitable), consistent on Transistor's inclusion; Transistor's own page is the primary citation used.
